title: Step By Step
eyebrow: Proposal · every screen drawn · nothing built yet

short.lead: The app failed QA because it shows too much at once. This plan keeps every feature and asks one question per screen. This version draws every screen and step, 83 of them, as a clickable prototype you can tap through, and every button, field and line of text is now a real desk object. Labels and kinds of work are a carousel, like projects. I checked all 125 things the app does today against it, and each one has a screen. The pictures and the prototype are drawings. Nothing is built yet, and your app hasn't changed.
short.hint: Tap each row to see its picture.
items: Four sources agree. The W3C guide for people with cognitive and learning disabilities says: 'Make Each Step Clear', 'Avoid Too Much Content', 'Make Short Critical Paths', 'Limit Interruptions' and 'Let Users Go Back'. GOV.UK's form standard says to start with one thing per page, because people focus on one answer, recover from mistakes more easily and cope better on a phone. GOV.UK's autism poster says 'Build simple and consistent layouts' and 'Don't build complex and cluttered layouts'. St Andrews' ADHD guidance says to show fewer tasks and options at once, reveal details only when they're needed, and show progress so you don't have to remember where you were.

Check that these rules match how the app feels to you. Sources: w3.org/TR/coga-usable, gov.uk/service-manual/design/form-structure, designnotes.blog.gov.uk ('One thing per page'), digitalcommunications.wp.st-andrews.ac.uk (designing for users with ADHD, and for autistic users).

I opened all 20 screens, panels and dialogs on a phone-sized screen and counted what you can press without scrolling. The busiest five are: Focus before you pick a project (54 things to press), the labels step in Sort (53), Task details (53), Milestone settings (50), and Sort after you pick a project (49). Every screen also starts with the same 14: the header icons, the jot box, the All / Area / Project switch and the five tabs. Those take up the top 40% of a phone screen. Your work starts below them. Settings (10) and the welcome screen (7) are already calm. The counts and pictures are in docs/generated/friction-map/.
Look at the picture and tell me if any screen I missed bothers you too.

items: Every screen in this page is also in a clickable prototype, published as the page 'Step by step prototype' (its link is in the chat, not in the repo). Tap a button and it goes where the real app would go. The list on the left jumps to any of the 83 screens. It is a drawing, not the app, so nothing you tap changes your tasks.
Open the prototype on your phone and try sorting one thought from start to finish.
All 125 things the app does today have a home

I listed every action the app can do today, 125 of them, straight from the app's code, and gave each one a screen in the prototype. A check script fails if any action has no screen, or points to a screen that doesn't exist. It passes. Two features I had left out of the first drawings are back: 'Part of a bigger task' and 'Subtasks', which are in today's third Sort step, and the due-date warning ('When should it warn you?'). Settings, the welcome and sync setup are unchanged, because they are already calm. The full list is in docs/generated/friction-steps/feature-map.json.
If you use something that isn't on any screen here, tell me its name.
Every control is a real object

No plain buttons are left. Each kind of control has one desk object, the same on every screen, and they match the objects the app already has (folders, index cards, the sticky note, jotter slips). The next step is an ink-stamped card. Back is a page corner folded back. Skip and links are sticky flags. A choice is an index card, and the one you picked gets a paperclip. Priority is coloured page flags, due dates are tear-off calendar pages, and status, Looks good and Done are rubber stamps. Tidy up keeps things in a tray, closes them in a bin and merges them with a stapler. Search is a magnifying glass, typing goes on a jotter strip, the check screen is a till receipt you change in pencil, and menus are a card-index drawer. Every question sits on a clipboard, the tabs are ring-binder dividers, and 'Showing' is label-maker tape.
Check that each object reads as what it does. Tell me any that don't.

items: The header keeps the name, + Jot (your pick), a sync dot and the cog. + Jot opens a screen with only the box; 'Goes to' picks Sort or a project, like today's To: stamp. The one 'Showing' line opens the All / Area / Project switch in a panel that slides up. The sync dot opens Sync now.
Check that a sync dot is enough in place of the sync button.

items: Your order, with the two link steps from today put back: project, priority, labels, due date (with an optional 'when to warn you'), part of, subtasks, waits on, holds up, then check. Priority can't be skipped; every other step after it has Skip. The ⋯ on the thought holds Add notes, Done already, Later and Delete. Labels are now a carousel of index cards, like projects: you flip through them and tap to pick, a paperclip marks each one you picked, and the picked ones collect as tags underneath. Find narrows the cards, 'A to Z' opens the card drawer, and the last card is '+ New label'. Project has '+ New project'. The check screen shows every answer with Change.
Check that nine steps isn't too long. If it is, option 2 of the first choice below offers a shorter way.

items: Today's 'Select many' becomes five steps: tick the thoughts (Tick all, Clear ticks), one project, labels, group them under one task, check. Priority and due dates stay one task at a time, as today.
Check that grouping under one task is worth its own step.

items.alt: Five phone screens of sorting several thoughts
items.caption: Select many, as five steps.

items: Organize starts by naming its two jobs. Tidy up shows one task at a time with its reason: waiting for review, replaced by newer work (it shows what replaced it), looks the same as another (both shown, Keep both or Merge), and not touched in 60 days. Nothing closes until the confirm screen, and Undo follows. Triage shows Now; Next and Later open on their own screens; 'Move…' turns on the move arrows and a 'Reset to the rules' button; 'Why these?' lists the seven real rules from the app.
Check that the Tidy up reasons read clearly one at a time.

items: All projects, and a new project

The project list keeps Find, progress bars and ways to sort (A to Z, most open tasks, closest deadline, recently synced, my own order with arrows). A new project is four steps: name, area, colour, then GitHub (not on GitHub, link one of my repos, create a new repo, or track someone else's repo).
Check that GitHub as the last optional step suits you.

items.alt: Eleven phone screens of the project list and a new project
items.caption: All projects and New project.

items: One milestone and one column at a time, with Previous, Next and All milestones. The ⋯ holds milestone settings, all milestones and sections (open, hide, reorder, add), find a task, edit project, sync and new project. Tapping a task opens what you can do to it: start it, send to review, mark done, move to another milestone, focus on this, make it a milestone, details. '+ Add a task' adds by name, or 'Add details…' runs the Sort steps. Milestone settings is two steps, with extra screens for entering your own number and for a checklist. Edit project is a list of lines that each open their step; Remove asks first.
Check that the ⋯ menu doesn't hide something you use every day.

items.alt: Fifteen phone screens of one project on the Roadmap
items.caption: One project, its menu, tasks and milestone settings.

items: Task details stops folding things away. It lists status, priority, due, labels, part of, subtasks, waits on, holds up, notes and GitHub, each with its answer. Tapping a line opens the same question the Sort step uses, with Save instead of Next. Subtasks and the GitHub issue get their own screens. ⋯ More holds rename, move to another project and delete.
Check that ten lines at once is calm enough; it scrolls a little on a phone.

items.alt: Five phone screens of task details
items.caption: Task details and its parts.

items: Which project (or Pick for me), then what kind of work (Skip means any; Unlabelled and Surprise me are in the folders). Kinds of work are index cards, as in the app today. Then one task on its sticky note, with two rubber stamps: 'I've done it' and 'Not this one'. The More button lists: start it, subtasks (tick, or tap to focus on one), details, go to the project, and clear. When you finish, the note peels away as today and you pick again.
Check that More is the right place for Start it.
Review asks 'Is it finished?' one task at a time, with two rubber stamps: Looks good or Needs more work, and Open details. Done this week keeps Undo on each task.
Check that one at a time suits Review too.

On a computer the tabs move to the left, the screen sits in a panel in the middle, and the list of steps sits beside it. A task's actions and its details open beside the list instead of over it, so you keep your place.
Check the desktop layout matches how you use the app on a computer.

choices: How should the optional Sort steps (labels to holds up) work?
Nine steps every time, but each optional one is one tap to skip. This is what the prototype shows.
Three steps by default (project, priority, check); the other six only if you tap 'Add more details?'.
I suggest asking each one, because you listed them as steps and Skip keeps it quick. Now that there are nine steps, option 2 is worth a look.
How should Tidy up show tasks?
Like flashcards: Keep or Close, then the next one.
A short list for each reason, with Keep and Close on each row.
I suggest one at a time, because it removes all the rows of buttons.

wrapup.summary: Every screen is now drawn, 83 in all, as pictures here and as a clickable prototype. All 125 things the app does today have a screen. Sort becomes nine steps, Task details one list, Focus two questions, Tidy up and Review one task at a time, and the Roadmap one milestone at a time.
wrapup.changing: Changed: how much each screen shows at once, Sort, adding a task, Focus, Tidy up, Triage, the Roadmap, Task details and Milestone settings. Kept: every feature, your data, the five tabs, Review and Settings.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your sign-off and your two remaining choices. The jot choice is already made: + Jot at the top.
wrapup.next: After you approve, I'll write the build plan as GitHub issues and build it on the same test link. Nothing goes into the app you use until you've tested it.
